title: Hyperscaler nuclear demand growing in tight uranium market
gist: Google's 20-year Constellation PPA and the Amazon/AEP/X-energy Xe-100 study show hyperscaler nuclear demand starting to register in a uranium market where mined supply already falls short; volumes are small but growing. The article is truncated by a paywall.

insights.claim: Hyperscaler nuclear procurement is beginning to affect uranium demand, but volumes are still small, in a market where mined supply already falls short of demand.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Incremental demand layered on a structural uranium supply deficit supports a bullish bias on uranium miners and fuel-cycle names.
insights.quote: Volumes are small but growing in a market where mined supply already falls short.

insights.claim: Google signed a 20-year power purchase agreement with Constellation on 6 October, funding more than USD 4.3 billion of upgrades across 11 units in Illinois, New Jersey and Pennsylvania to add 890MW.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Hyperscalers are financing capacity additions at existing reactors; watch Constellation's uprate pipeline.

insights.claim: Google also signed a 15-year deal for 2,700MW from existing Constellation nuclear plants, locking in long-dated baseload for data centers.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Long-tenor offtake of existing nuclear tightens merchant supply and supports nuclear generator valuations.

insights.claim: On 19 October Amazon, AEP and X-energy agreed to study a 960MW, 12-reactor plant using the advanced Xe-100 design at a former Indiana coal site, ahead of any final investment decision.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: This is a study, not an FID; SMR/advanced-reactor uranium (HALEU) demand remains optional until a decision is taken.
